trigger.snippet: | `melian doctor` | Checks Node, git and `--attr-source`, Pi's login, providers with credentials, the GitHub token's source, gh, and the repository. It names which `melian` ran and warns when it lies inside the checkout. The `clone` line names the linked git clone, its commit, and whether its tree is clean. It warns when the clone is dirty or git cannot read it. An install under `node_modules` omits that line. Doctor also checks the state directory and whether it is writable. Its `records` line, when the checkout has an `origin`, fetches the `melian/state` branch's tip into the store's own repository. It names, as a warning, up to five files on it that Melian did not write, which refuse calls until a writer removes them, or warns that the branch cannot be read. Opening the store sweeps what killed calls left in the state directory, and the line warns about what that sweep left: up to five leftovers it kept because it cannot tell their maker is gone, up to five of an exited call it could not remove, how many stale ones it ran out of time to remove, or left because it could not list every leftover, which the next open removes, that it stopped listing at its bound of 1,000 leftovers, and a process table it could not read, which sweeps nothing and keeps every leftover it found. It names them after the branch's own warning when the branch cannot be read, since the sweep ran when the store opened. A sweep that removed all it found says nothing. The same line then says whom the committed root policy trusts to write the branch. It reads `trust.writers` from the same base as the `trust` line. With it on, the line says the branch's writers are trusted as the repository's writers. With it off, it warns that only the trusted host may write `melian/state`, since doctor cannot check who may push to it. When no policy can be read, it warns that who may write the branch is unknown. A policy read from local `main` or `HEAD` makes the line a warning, with the `trust` line's caveat. Doctor reads the cached remote-tracking ref and never fetches it. So a clone that has not fetched reports the policy as of its last fetch, and each of the two lines names the ref and commit it read. [Issue #491](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/491) would check that commit against the remote. It never pushes and never fails. It also checks the named credentials of the secrets files, failing when git tracks `melian.local.yaml` or `melian.secrets.yaml` or a secrets file cannot be read, and warning for one others can read. It checks whether each lens's levels cost more from `quick` to `deep`, warning for a level on a lighter tier or with a smaller token or tool budget than the level below it. Its `resolution` lines list, for each `melian.yaml` and preference file in the working tree, every farther value and lens default its `resolution` overrides, or say that none does. It checks whether Biome and tsc come from the checkout or Melian's own copy. Its `probes` line runs an empty probe and says whether probes run here, or why every probe is refused, as a warning. Each manifest tool has a readiness line: materialised and verified, not yet fetched, unavailable, or manifest mismatch. `unavailable` marks a platform with no pin or a cache path that cannot be inspected, and doctor reports it as a warning. Doctor never downloads or runs a manifest tool; a mismatch fails doctor. Its standards line counts regular standards files and their bytes at every depth, warns for oversized files and skipped symlinks, and lists at most ten paths. Its `decision index` line gives the size of the decision index at `HEAD`, and warns past 64 KiB, with the warning `melian review` gives, or when the decisions cannot be read; it never fails. Its `routes` line names each tier’s resolved provider/model route and status, including the verifier. It also prints the review plan it would resolve now, as `plan` lines, from the working tree and the preference files. A pull request's review reads its policy and lenses from its base and no preference file. So a `plan` warning names each preference file doctor read, and every key it sets, from the loader's own list. It leaves out `output`, which every review reads from the preference files to render. Problem: on [pull request #532](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/532) a lens route in `melian.local.yaml` printed as applying. Two pull request rounds ran on the committed model before anyone knew. Doctor takes no pull request argument and never fetches, so it cannot print a pull request's own plan. The warning is what it can say. Each routed tier shows its models, the credential each comes from, and the file that routed it, or that it was derived. Each lens's levels show the tier and model of each, and a lens with its own route has a `route` line and shows each level on the lens route. Every warning appears too. A tier with no route names the lenses that use it and the ways to fix it. Other warnings name missing credentials, a tier policy refuses, a route off the committed one, or a route model the catalogue does not hold, with the file that set it and, for an unknown provider, the provider. It fails with its own `decisions` line when `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider` | `0`, or `1` when Node or git cannot run a review, `melian.yaml` sets `decisions.provider`, git tracks a file only a maintainer may hold, a secrets file cannot be read, or a named credential's provider is unknown or accepts neither API keys nor OAuth tokens, or a manifest tool mismatches its pin |
